articles.title: In 2026, Stephen Curry accepted a $116 million Warriors extension around $20 million below his maximum
articles.summary: Stephen Curry could have asked the Golden State Warriors for every dollar available to him.
articles.body: Stephen Curry could have asked the Golden State Warriors for every dollar available to him. Instead, the four-time NBA champion agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension in September 2026, choosing a deal worth roughly $20 million less than his reported maximum. The decision was about more than a new contract. At 38, Curry wants another championship, a competitive team around him and the chance to end his career with the franchise that drafted him in 2009. His choice also gives Golden State more room to plan its next moves as it tries to remain a serious contender in the Western Conference.Stephen Curry accepts a $116 million Warriors extensionThe Warriors confirmed the extension on September 26, securing Stephen Curry's future with the franchise for two more seasons. The agreement is expected to keep him in Golden State through the 2028-29 campaign, potentially carrying him into his 20th NBA season with the same team.According to an Associated Press report published by NBA.com, Curry could have commanded a maximum deal worth about $136 million over two years. The reported $116 million agreement therefore represented a substantial concession, although the final financial difference depends on how the contract's player option is counted.Curry explained his thinking during the Warriors' media day, making it clear that the decision involved several possible outcomes rather than a simple choice between two salary figures.“Yes, I was presented the max,” Curry said Monday at media day, “yes, there was everything on the table.”He also described the discussions as a process that required both sides to consider his personal interests and the team's future.“It was a very, kind of, thoughtful journey, partnership of putting all the different scenarios out there. It was of interest of making sure I was here, figuring out what was in the best setup for me, for the team, for the now, for the flexibility the rest of my career,” Curry said.The agreement gives Curry another opportunity to compete with the Warriors while allowing the front office to consider how it can improve the roster around him. It also removes uncertainty about his immediate future, an important step for a franchise built around his shooting, leadership and long-standing connection with its supporters.Why Stephen Curry took less money from the WarriorsStephen Curry's decision reflects the challenge facing an established star in the later stages of his career. He remains one of the NBA's most dangerous offensive players, but another championship will require a strong supporting cast and a team capable of handling the demands of a long season.The Warriors cannot rely on Curry alone to carry them through every round of the playoffs. They need consistent contributions from their other starters, dependable depth and enough flexibility to respond when injuries or changes in form affect the lineup.Taking less money can help create options, although it does not guarantee that Golden State will sign another star or build a championship roster. The front office must still identify suitable players, manage future contracts and decide which moves offer the best chance of success.Curry acknowledged that the team's recent history and future ambitions played a role in his decision.“So trying to balance all of that is such a unique situation with all of the circumstances of where we’ve been the last four years, what’s currently on the table and where we’re trying to go to be competitive and give ourselves a chance.”His words point to a practical goal: give the Warriors a better chance to compete without sacrificing the stability of a partnership that has defined much of his career.General manager Mike Dunleavy also praised Curry's commitment. In his statement announcing the extension, Dunleavy said, “We couldn’t be more excited about reaching an agreement with Stephen and extending his historic career with the Warriors.”Dunleavy described Curry as an exceptional representative of the franchise, highlighting his leadership, performance and impact in the community. The comments show why the agreement matters beyond its financial terms. Curry remains central to the team's identity, and both sides have a shared interest in keeping that relationship intact.The contract gives the Warriors more flexibilityStephen Curry's extension could influence several important decisions over the next two seasons. Golden State must balance its desire to compete now with the need to prepare for the period when its veteran core begins to change.Draymond Green is one of the key figures in that discussion. The longtime teammate has been part of the Warriors' championship success alongside Curry, and retaining experienced players could help the team remain competitive.Curry acknowledged that the possibility of keeping familiar teammates was part of the broader conversation. However, the extension does not guarantee that Green or any other player will remain with Golden State. Contract terms, roster needs and the team's financial position will all affect future decisions.The deal also includes a player option for the 2028-29 season, according to reporting by the San Francisco Chronicle. That provision gives Curry another decision point after the 2026-27 season and could affect how much flexibility the Warriors have in the years ahead.The option matters because Curry is not simply committing to a salary. He is also keeping control over part of his future. If the Warriors make the roster improvements he wants, he could continue with the franchise. If the team's direction changes, the option could give him another opportunity to assess his choices.Golden State's front office now faces the challenge of turning that financial room into meaningful improvement. It must judge whether to retain existing players, pursue outside talent or give younger members of the roster larger roles.A smaller contract for Curry may make those choices easier, but the team's decisions on the court will ultimately determine whether the move pays off.Stephen Curry wants to finish his career with Golden StateStephen Curry's relationship with the Warriors stretches back to 2009, when the franchise selected him with the seventh overall pick in the NBA Draft. His early career included questions about his size and durability, but he went on to become one of the greatest shooters in basketball history.He helped transform the Warriors into a modern NBA powerhouse, winning four championships and earning two regular-season MVP awards. His shooting range changed how teams defend the perimeter, while his partnership with Green and other teammates helped define Golden State's championship era.The new extension offers Curry a chance to add another chapter to that story. It also reflects his connection with the Bay Area, where he has spent his entire professional career.Speaking about his decision, Curry put that connection simply: “This is a community that I’ve played in front of my entire career, and being able to finish the story the right way is a big part of, I think, what I can control thankfully, and hopefully health-wise as well,” he said.His words capture the personal side of the agreement. Curry has earned the right to pursue the largest possible contract, yet he has chosen a route that may help his team build a stronger supporting cast.That does not mean the Warriors are guaranteed another title. The Western Conference remains difficult, and roster health, defensive consistency and the performance of younger players will all matter. Curry's own availability will be important, too, particularly after he was limited to 43 games in the 2025-26 season because of a right knee injury, according to NBA.com.Still, the extension gives Golden State a clear foundation for the next stage of its plans. Curry remains committed to the team, and the Warriors have an opportunity to make the most of his remaining prime years.The $116 million agreement is therefore more than a headline about a pay cut. It is a decision shaped by loyalty, ambition and the realities of team building. Stephen Curry has secured his place in Golden State for the near future. Now the Warriors must show that the financial flexibility he helped create can bring them closer to another championship.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “We grew up here as adults”: Stephen Curry reflects on his bond with Oakland as he and Ayesha Curry continue their charitable mission
articles.summary: Stephen Curry, the four time NBA champion, and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have stood by the children of Oakland for the last decade.
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the four time NBA champion, and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have stood by the children of Oakland for the last decade. Ahead of the new season, the Golden State Warriors’ star player Stephen Curry has opened up about their commitment to Oakland as they continue to change thousands of lives.Stephen Curry opens up about his and wife Ayesha Curry’s dedication to Oakland as they change lives thereA few weeks ago, in an interview, Stephen Curry reflected on his and Ayesha Curry's contribution as they said, “You have a voice. You have everything that you need to make a true impact. And I encourage you to find your Oakland. Find what makes you different and where you can have that impact.”The two time league MVP added, “I had a feeling that, you know, this was hopefully a place that we would be around for a long time. But to your point, the bond with a community that supported us from, you know, day one, through some rough times on the court, but always, great energy and pride to represent Oakland when we were over at Oracle. All those things matter to us…”The four time NBA champion also reflected on how Oakland has shaped them as he said, “We talk about it a lot. Like, we grew up pretty much here as adults. I was 21 when I got drafted. She was 20. Like, now, almost 18 years later, to the point of just that bond growing now to what, you know, Eat. Learn. Play. is and being able to plant our flag in Oakland…”Stephen Curry added, “That call to action was everybody has a place of impact, a circle of influence that they have. We’ve been blessed with a very, very, you know, big platform to do it. And, you know, show up and find your ways to make somebody else’s life just a little bit better.”Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have raised millions for Eat, Learn & PlayStephen Curry and his wife. Ayesha Curry, have invested their own funds into their charity, Eat, Learn & Play, when they were initially setting it up in 2018.Since then, both of them have remained dedicated towards the children of Oakland as they have continued to provide access to quality education, nutritious meals and have also encouraged more sports participation among children.The Eat, Learn & Play has also built hundreds of playgrounds across schools around Oakland as they have raised a whopping $100 million for their charity in the last eight years.For now, Stephen Curry focuses on the new season as he trains with the Golden State Warriors while he eyes a win this time.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: LeBron James’ son Bronny James’ 0-point preseason performance could decide playing minutes in Lakers’ regular season
articles.summary: Bronny James played 11 minutes against the Warriors on Tuesday and did not score a single point.
articles.body: Bronny James played 11 minutes against the Warriors on Tuesday and did not score a single point. He missed both shots, turned the ball over four times and finished with a team-worst minus-18 in a 101-89 Lakers loss. It was his fourth preseason game of a third NBA season, and the numbers across all four look just as rough. Los Angeles also has 16 guaranteed contracts, one above the regular-season limit, so a move is coming before opening night. Coach JJ Redick has already said the 22-year-old has not played well in the four preseason games.Is Bronny James struggling in the NBA preseason?Yes, and Tuesday’s game made the case on its own. With Luka Doncic resting and Collin Sexton sidelined, Bronny James got the extra ball-handling minutes. He shot 0-for-2, grabbed one rebound, added one steal and committed four turnovers in 11 minutes. The Lakers held a double-digit lead at halftime, and James still posted the worst plus-minus on the roster.It was not a case of too few chances. James has played extended minutes in all four exhibition games. The one bright spot came against Sacramento last Thursday, when the guard put up 4 points, 4 rebounds, 6 assists and a steal in 22 minutes of a 114-110 win.Fans are worried about the Lakers guard. However, not everyone has given up on him. A league source who spoke with NBC Sports at Summer League offered a different read, saying “He might stick.” Preseason results swing hard in both directions, and the Lakers have yet to play game one of 82.What are Bronny James’ preseason stats?Through four games, Bronny James is averaging 2.8 points and 3.3 assists in 17.5 minutes a night. He is shooting 26.7% from the field and 14.3% from three, and he is giving the ball away 3.0 times per game.The climb from year one to year two was steady. His minutes went from 6.7 to 8.9, his scoring from 2.3 to 2.9 and his field goal rate from 31.3% to 40.9%. Over the two seasons combined he averaged 2.7 points on 37.4% shooting, with 0.4 steals and 0.1 blocks a game.The preseason has reversed the shooting gains. The $2.3 million guard is playing about twice as many minutes as he did in 2025-26, 17.5 against 8.9, yet his scoring is flat at 2.8 against 2.9. That works out to roughly 0.16 points a minute, down from about 0.33. The three-point shot has fallen furthest, from 38.6% to 14.3%. Assists are the one number moving the right way, up from 1.2 to 3.3, which fits a larger ball-handling role.What did JJ Redick say about Bronny James’ poor performance?Redick made his stance on Bronny James with a brutal remark. After the Warriors loss, the Lakers coach said, “I don’t think he has played well in the four preseason games.” He had kind words for the stretch before that, calling September and the summer really nice for James, and he added that “he’s had good practices.”He also pushed part of the blame outward. Some of it is rhythm, Redick said, and some of it is who James plays with. The guard has logged a lot of second-half minutes beside the team’s two-way players, and the coach said that group is not necessarily setting him up for success. The game backs that up in part. Los Angeles was in control while the regulars played, then lost the second half 51-26 once the reserves carried the load.Redick has listed James, Jaden Hardy and Chris Mañon as the three players who would handle the ball when either Doncic or Sexton is out. His explanation was short: “we need another ball-handler.” The coach has also said the Lakers cannot ask Doncic and Austin Reaves to carry ball-handling duties through an 82-game season. Those comments make the backup job a real one, and Tuesday was a live test of it.The night itself shows where the focus sat. Reaves scored 28, and Walker Kessler looked good in his preseason debut, yet most of the attention went to James.Both of Redick’s points can be true. Lineups and rhythm explain some of a poor shooting stretch. Turnovers are harder to hand to teammates, and James has 12 of them in four games, one more than the 11 points he has scored.What must Bronny James do to earn playing minutes?Cutting the turnovers comes first. James is a combo guard rather than a natural point guard, and his value has been as a two-way disruptor, but Redick’s own words show ball-handling is part of the job on nights Doncic or Sexton sits. He is competing with Hardy and Mañon for it.The three-point shot has to come back too. The gap from last season’s 38.6% is more than 24 points. Occasional defensive energy will not be enough on its own, and he should look sharper against fellow fringe-roster players, the way he did in the G League. California Post columnist Melissa Rohlin wrote Wednesday that James needs significant improvement to build his own identity and win a meaningful role.The roster math adds pressure. The Lakers hold 16 guaranteed standard contracts against a limit of 15, and president Rob Pelinka must trade or waive someone before the season starts. James, Hardy and Dalton Knecht have all come up in that talk, though nothing points to James as the preferred cut. His $2.3 million for 2026-27 is guaranteed, and the Lakers hold a $2.5 million team option for 2027-28. Friday’s preseason finale against Denver is the last exhibition chance to change the picture.Does LeBron James’ absence affect Bronny James?It appears to be. This is Bronny’s first season without LeBron on the roster after the move to Philadelphia. Last spring the two shared the floor in playoff minutes, mostly in the first-round series win over Houston.Dan Woike, answering a fan Q&A Thursday, said the Lakers knew drafting Bronny would make LeBron happy but have long liked his athleticism and length, and they have raved about his work ethic. “The belief in Bronny James the person/player is genuine,” Woike wrote. Belief only goes so far without production, and the argument for keeping James now rests on his own game. articles.title: Amar'e Stoudemire, Naismith Basketball Hall of Famer, graduates from Miami police academy
articles.summary: Stoudemire was a 6-time NBA All-Star. Then he was an assistant coach in the league. Now he's entering the next chapter of his career.
articles.body:
Amar'e Stoudemire is among the most accomplished basketball players of his generation: He won NBA Rookie of the Year in 2003, then went on to become a six-time All-Star in a 14-season career that earned him a spot in the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame this summer .

Many might remember Stoudemire as a Phoenix Sun. Others may think of him as a New York Knick.

But, as of Wednesday, Stoudemire is something completely different: a police officer.

The former frontcourt standout and Brooklyn Nets assistant coach graduated from the Miami Dade College School of Justice's Basic Law Enforcement Academy this week.

Stoudemire, 43, will work with the county's school police department.

"For Amar'e, this is more than a second career," the school said in a post on X . "Becoming a police officer was a childhood dream, inspired in part by family members who served in law enforcement.

"Now, he will begin a new chapter as a police officer with the Miami-Dade Schools Police Department, giving back to our community and serving as a positive influence for the next generation."

The school also noted that Stoudemire received the Harry "Coach" Everett Award "for his contributions to the success of the academy program throughout his training."

Stoudemire was part of a Hall of Fame class that included his longtime coach, Mike D'Antoni. Together, they enjoyed success in Phoenix and New York.

As Miami-Dade College referenced in its social media post on Wednesday, Stoudemire played for the Heat as well. That was at the end of his illustrious career, after he made a brief stop with the Dallas Mavericks.

Over the years , the 6-foot-10 Stoudemire averaged 18.9 points and 7.8 boards. In 2010-11, his first season with the Knicks, he posted 25.3 points per game as New York returned to the playoffs for the first time in seven years. Long before that, in 2004-05, he put up a career-high 26 points per contest for a Suns team that won 62 regular-season games and reached the Western Conference Finals.

Steve Nash won NBA MVP that season, and Stoudemire wound up coaching under him with the Nets from 2020 to 2022.

Despite all of his exploits on the hardwood, Stoudemire still had another dream to live out.

"It's something I always wanted to do since I was a kid," Stoudemire said of becoming a police officer in an interview with Sports Illustrated .

"I remember back when I was in grade school, elementary school. They asked you on career day, 'What do you want to be when you grow up?' And my initial response was a police officer. It runs in the family. My uncle was a captain. His brother was a deputy. My cousin is a captain. My sister's in the academy. So, it's a family tradition, basically."

articles.title: “Aura peaked”: Luka Doncic’s latest $5 million move sends fans into a frenzy as Lakers star drives Bugatti to practice
articles.summary: Luka Doncic pulled into Lakers practice on Thursday in one of the rarest cars on the road.
articles.body: Luka Doncic pulled into Lakers practice on Thursday in one of the rarest cars on the road. The Bugatti Mistral is valued at about $5 million, only 99 were built, and it is the fastest open-top production road car on record. Video of the arrival spread fast online, and fans had plenty to say about it. Los Angeles plays Denver in its preseason finale on Friday and opens the season against Golden State on Oct. 21, so the Lakers guard gave the team a talking point before any real games count.Luka Doncic shows off his $5 million Bugatti as he drives to Lakers practiceLuka Doncic arrived in a Bugatti W16 Mistral, the newest addition to his collection. The 27-year-old Slovenian has been open about the hobby. Doncic spoke about cars at length in an interview with Sports Illustrated released Oct. 8.The Mistral tops out at 282 mph, or 454 km/h. As of November 2025, the garage held 15 cars, with the Mistral the newest. Snoop Dogg checked it out last November. The known list also includes a Koenigsegg Regera, a Rimac Nevera, a Ferrari 812 Superfast, a Brabus Rocket 1000, a Lamborghini Urus, a 1967 Ford Bronco and a Zastava 750.The car is a side note to the day job. Doncic averaged 33.5 points, 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists in 64 games last season while shooting 47.6% from the field and 36.6% from three. The reigning scoring champion landed on the All-NBA First Team again and placed fourth in MVP voting.How are fans reacting to Luka Doncic’s Bugatti arrival?Reaction came quickly on social media, and most of it was short and punchy. Helluva Ball Club (@Letweet23) posted, “Aura peaked.” IRE “SCHOTTY” (@TheWalkingDad69) went bigger with “MVP and Finals MVP.” Steven Gonzalez (@sixspeedsteve) wrote, “Probably so much fun to drive in LA.” Yosemite Damn (@WrittenbyHR) went with a superhero line: “He got that Bruce Wayne.”InfanityTV (@InfanityTV) called the entrance on-brand and recalled a JJ Redick story about a private plane for 14 to 16 guys headed to Slovenia. The post summed it up as pretty extra.The respect is not limited to fans. In the annual NBA GM Survey released Thursday, general managers voted Doncic the best small forward, 37 percent to Jayson Tatum’s 33. The Lakers star also placed third at point guard and third at shooting guard. Redick uses Doncic as a point guard on offense and a forward on defense, so the labels keep shifting. Not every coach gets a player who can fill just about any spot except center.Doncic and the Lakers face Denver at Crypto.com Arena on Friday, then get a few days off before hosting Golden State on Wednesday, Oct. 21.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: LeBron James’ Fanatics partnership fuels new questions about his 76ers move as Pablo Torre shares league sources’ suspicions
articles.summary: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, has sparked heated discussions across communities ever since he was spotted taking a helicopter ride to
articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, has sparked heated discussions across communities ever since he was spotted taking a helicopter ride to arrive at the Philadelphia 76ers’ training sessions from his home in New York City. Later, it was reported that the helicopter that the NBA icon has been using for transportation is included in his contract with the Fanatics. Amid this, there have been new speculations.Pablo Torre weighs in on whether LeBron James’ deal with the Philadelphia 76ers had anything to do with FanaticsA few hours ago, in an interview with Front Office Sports live event Tuned In, hosted by reporter Daniel Roberts, Pablo Torre said, "League sources have been wondering if former Sixers minority owner Michael Rubin flipped LeBron — convinced him to sign with the Sixers at Fanatics Fest…”The popular journalist added, “When we asked Sixers PR for comment, they didn't reply."Interestingly, the Fanatics CEO Michael Rubin was a minority stakeholder in the Philadelphia 76ers.Michael Rubin bought his minority stake in the Philadelphia 76ers in October 2011. He was part of the original investment group, led by Josh Harris and David Blitzer, that acquired the team from Comcast Spectacor for $280 million. The NBA formally approved the transaction on October 13, 2011.Over the course of his 11 year run as a minority owner, he eventually consolidated his holdings into a 10% equity stake in Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment (HBSE) before divesting in 2022.However, there are no confirmations if it was Fanatics CEO Michael Rubin’s advice that led LeBron James to sign a deal with the Philadelphia 76ers.All about LeBron James’ expensive deal with Fanatics as he uses their helicopterFanatics officially signed LeBron James on January 10, 2024, ending his historic 20 year exclusive relationship with rival trading card company Upper Deck.The 41 year old NBA icon signed an exclusive multi-year partnership with Fanatics Collectibles (the trading card and memorabilia division). The deal kicked off with a rare dual-autograph card featuring both LeBron and his son, Bronny James.While speculations continue about his move to the Philadelphia 76ers, LeBron James had made it clear why he joined the team.A few weeks ago, in a social media post, he wrote, "This is my last decision. I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice," James said. "I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship. I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time. Thank you LA. articles.title: Aday Mara se baja de los dobles dígitos y se mantiene máximo en los Thunder: "Es un monstruo"
articles.standfirst: Aday Mara fue el mejor reboteador de los Thunder y estuvo más eficiente que Isaiah Hartenstein, el pívot con el que se juega los minutos
articles.summary: Aday Mara fue el mejor reboteador de los Thunder y estuvo más eficiente que Isaiah Hartenstein, el pívot con el que se juega los minutos
articles.body: Los Oklahoma City Thunder de Aday Mara perdieron 116-89 ante los Houston Rockets en un partido de la pretemporada NBA. El pívot español de 21 años y 2,21 m. de altura, y que oficialmente tiene una envergadura de 2,29 m. y un histórico alcance de 2,97 m., firmó 6 puntos (3 de 4 en tiros de 2), 9 rebotes, 2 asistencias y 1 tapón en 21 minutos. Aday Mara fue el máximo reboteador de los Thunder, pero por primera vez en sus cinco partidos de pretemporada se bajó de los dobles dígitos (12 puntos el primer partido, 22 puntos el segundo, 17 puntos el tercero y 10 puntos en el cuarto). En su particular duelo por los minutos en pista en el Toyota Center con su compañero Isaiah Hartenstein, llamado a ser el pívot titular de Mark Daigneault, el 'center' internacional con Alemania sumó 6 puntos y 8 rebotes en 19 puntos. Con Hartenstein en pista los Thunder tuvieron un +/- de -16, mientras que con Aday Mara el +/- fue de -9. Ajay Mitchell, escolta belga de los Thunder, confesó antes del partido que "Aday Mara es un monstruo. No sabía que era tan habilidoso ofensivamente". Los jugadores más destacados de la franquicia de Oklahoma City fueron Jalen Williams (18 puntos) y Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (17 puntos). Kevin Durant (11 puntos en 16 minutos), Alperen Sengun (14 puntos), Amen Thompson (12 puntos), Tari Eason (12 puntos), Reed Sheppard (11 puntos) y Bogdan Bogdanovic (15 puntos) firmaron dobles dígitos en los Rockets.

articles.title: New Lakers Rumors Reveal Potential Dalton Knecht Trade Landing Spot as LA Tries to Cut Down Roster
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have discussed trading Dalton Knecht to the Milwaukee Bucks in exchange for center Jericho Sims, according to NBA insider Jake Fischer.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have discussed trading Dalton Knecht to the Milwaukee Bucks in exchange for center Jericho Sims, according to NBA insider Jake Fischer .

"League sources say that the Lakers and Bucks have held exploratory trade discussions on a framework that would ship former first-round selection Dalton Knecht to Milwaukee (along with second-round draft capital) in exchange for big man Jericho Sims," Fischer reported Thursday. "Yet it must be said that I've also heard some pessimism from sources briefed on those talks that such a trade will actually go through."

On Monday, teams are required to cut their rosters down to 15 players.

Fischer noted that the Lakers may be forced to waive Knecht if they aren't able to trade him, as they currently have 16 players with standard contracts on their roster.

The 25-year-old was initially selected by Los Angeles with the No. 17 overall pick in the 2024 NBA draft.

Knecht showed promise as a rookie, averaging 9.1 points and 2.8 rebounds in 19.2 minutes per game while shooting 46.1 percent from the field and 37.6 percent from three-point territory.

He fell out of the Lakers' rotation during his 2025-26 campaign, though.

Knecht recorded just 4.2 points and 1.4 rebounds per game while connecting on 45.5 percent of his field goals and 34.2 percent of his triples.

His defense was an issue, as his minus-8.5 net rating was the worst mark among all Lakers players to appear in at least 30 games last season (via NBA.com ).

After Los Angeles improved its wing depth by bringing in players such as Quentin Grimes, Jaden Hardy and Matisse Thybulle during the offseason, Knecht's days as a member of the organization may be numbered.

articles.title: What is Luka Doncic’s official new weight? Lakers star’s transformation result revealed ahead of regular season
articles.summary: Luka Doncic reported to Lakers training camp at 242 pounds, two fewer than a year ago, according to Jovan Buha of The Athletic.
articles.body: Luka Doncic reported to Lakers training camp at 242 pounds, two fewer than a year ago, according to Jovan Buha of The Athletic. The number lands at an awkward time. NBA general managers gave Doncic zero MVP votes in a new preseason survey, and Los Angeles opens against Golden State on Oct. 21. LeBron James has left for Philadelphia. A fresh group of role players has arrived. A hamstring strain wiped out the Lakers star’s playoffs last spring, and the 27-year-old now heads into a ninth NBA season with plenty to prove.What is Luka Doncic’s current weight?Luka Doncic is officially listed at 242 pounds. Buha reported the figure this week, and it is a modest drop from the 244 pounds Doncic carried into last year’s camp. Small number, long project. The guard has been working on his conditioning since the summer of 2025 and even appeared on the cover of Men’s Health last year. An earlier offseason report said the six-time All-Star is about as lean as in the early years of an NBA career. With James gone, Doncic is the clear lead in Los Angeles, so the work matters. Doncic led the league with 33.5 points per game, a second scoring title, yet played only 64 regular season games. The hamstring strain from early April then cost the Slovenian every playoff game.Insider drops big news on Luka Doncic’s LakersThe Lakers are optimistic, but not all of it rests on firm ground. Golliver pointed to last season’s sweep in the conference semifinals, the surprise ownership change in August and two open spots in the starting lineup at the start of camp. On continuity, he wrote, the Lakers “clearly trail behind most of the leading title favorites.” Still, he sees a resemblance to the 2023-24 Mavericks now that center Walker Kessler is in place. Doncic led that Dallas team to 50 wins and a trip to the Finals. Those Mavs began the year with the 11th-shortest title odds, then added Daniel Gafford and P.J. Washington in midseason trades.JJ Redick responds to Doncic’s MVP snubJJ Redick did not take the bait when asked about the survey. Victor Wembanyama led the voting at 77%, with Nikola Jokic at 10% and Anthony Edwards at 7%. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jayson Tatum also drew votes. Doncic drew none, though the GMs did name him the league’s best small forward at 37%.Last season Doncic averaged 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists on top of the scoring title, then finished fourth in the final MVP rankings behind Gilgeous-Alexander, Jokic and Wembanyama. The injury drove that slide. In advance of their matchup against Nikola Jokic and crew, the Lakers made two small roster moves on Thursday. They reportedly waived forward Cole Swider, a 3-point specialist they had recently brought in on an Exhibit 10 contract. Swider had been with the Lakers in the past, both on their active roster and with their G League affiliate.

In three preseason games this month, he had a total of 11 points on 3-of-10 shooting, two rebounds and three assists.

Los Angeles also signed guard Jahmir Young, and subsequently waived him, per Dan Woike of The Athletic . The team also brought in forward Aniwaniwa Tait-Jones to an Exhibit 10 contract, per Olgun Uluc of ESPN . Tait-Jones is from New Zealand and averaged 15.9 points, 6.9 rebounds and 2.7 assists a game for Valmiera Glass VIA, a team in the Latvian-Estonian Basketball League Championship, while winning the league's final MVP last season.

He had previously spent two seasons at the University of California, San Diego, where he won Big West Player of the Year honors in 2025.

articles.title: Angel Reese vs. Caitlin Clark: How Dream star reached first championship appearance before Fever sensation
articles.summary: As members of the same draft class and longtime star rivals, Reese has now reached the WNBA's biggest stage before Clark.
articles.body:
At this point, Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark will forever be connected and compared to one another.

As college rivals, members of the same draft class and now as WNBA stars, Reese and Clark have been two of the faces of basketball over the last few years — sometimes, of course, for reasons far beyond their play on the court. But their intertwined careers, like many basketball player rivalries across history, mean their legacies and accolades are always being compared to one another.

While they're very different players stylistically, Reese didn't just beat Clark in the 2023 national title game to beat her counterpart to a college championship. Now, the Dream center has reached the WNBA Finals before Clark has, with a chance to add her first ring in the pros.

Here's a look at how Reese reached the WNBA Finals before Clark in their respective careers.

How Angel Reese got to WNBA championship before Caitlin Clark

Reese and Clark were members of the same draft class after decorated college careers. While Reese had something Clark did not in her college career — a national title — it was the Iowa guard who went No. 1 overall to the Fever after a Hawkeyes career loaded with individual awards and accolades.

Reese, meanwhile, landed with the Sky at No. 7 overall, where she became a focal piece in Chicago's frontcourt. Both players became massive instant upgrades for their franchise, but only one would last more than a few seasons with their first team.

After winning just 13 games the season prior, the addition of Clark helped Indiana become far more competitive, going an even 20-20 in her rookie season in 2024. Under coach Christie Sides, the Fever even snuck into the playoffs as the No. 6 seed, with Clark remaining a star right off the bat in the WNBA. She set the WNBA single-game record for assists (19), was named an All-Star, became the first rookie to record a triple-double, set the league rookie season assists and 3-pointers records, and was then named the Rookie of the Year.

Ultimately, Indiana's first playoff berth since 2016 was short-lived, swept by the Sun in the first round.

Reese's first year in Chicago, meanwhile, wasn't very successful from a team aspect. The Sky went just 13-27, the third-worst record in the WNBA, though Reese was one of their few bright spots. The young center was named an All-Star, had a three-game streak of 20-rebound performances, broke the WNBA single-season rebounding record and set a new league record with 13.1 rebounds per game.

Despite being two emerging young stars in the WNBA, neither Clark nor Reese wound up having the sophomore season they likely hoped for.

For Clark, it was injury issues that derailed her second season. She played in just 13 games due to quad, ankle and groin injuries, ruled out for the season by early September despite playing well when on the court, averaging 8.8 assists per game.

Even without Clark for a majority of the season, though, Indiana still had a successful season, making the playoffs as a No. 6 seed again and improving its win total to 24. Behind Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston, the Fever made a run to the semifinals in the playoffs, where they fell to the eventual champion Aces in overtime of a decisive Game 5. Clark wasn't playing, but her squad was on the verge of the WNBA Finals.

For Reese, the 2025 season was similar to 2024: individual success, but little wins to show for it. She recorded her first triple-double, was selected to the All-Star Game and led the WNBA in rebounding once again, but not only did the Sky go just 10-34 — Reese also dealt with off-the-court issues. Late in the season, she openly voiced frustrations about the team's performance, and the Sky suspended her for a half-game for making "statements detrimental to the team." Additionally, she had eight technical fouls, receiving another one-game suspension.

Compared to their sophomore WNBA campaigns, both Clark and Reese can argue that they enjoyed better third years — but for Reese, things have gone especially well since an exit from Chicago.

In April, Reese was traded by the Sky to the Dream in exchange for two first-round picks, giving her a much better opportunity to contend for a title after some tension in Chicago. In Atlanta, she remained the same double-double threat, named an All-Star this season for the third-straight year and becoming the fastest player in WNBA history to record 1,000 career rebounds. Reese set WNBA records for single-game rebounds (26) and single-season rebounds, going on to be named Defensive Player of the Year.

Clark, meanwhile, stayed healthy in 2026, enjoying 40 games on the court while averaging a career-high in points per game (22.3). Her return to the court helped Indiana improve its win total for the third-straight year, winning 28 games to claim the 6th seed once again. Clark was named an All-Star and set a new career-high with 45 points in a game, but ultimately, the Fever were eliminated by defending champion Aces in the first round.

Reese, meanwhile, has helped lead Atlanta past the Mystics and Liberty to reach her first WNBA Finals. If the Dream come out on top, it will mean that Reese has won a championship in high school, college, Unrivaled and the WNBA.

Reese and Clark were both drafted in 2024.

articles.title: La NBA más despiadada: Dallas despide al español Guillermo Díaz-Graham... ¡para fichar a su hermano gemelo Jorge!
articles.standfirst: Ambos podría acabar jugando juntos en los Texas Legends de la G League
articles.summary: Ambos podría acabar jugando juntos en los Texas Legends de la G League
articles.body: Los Dallas Mavericks ficharon al español Guillermo Díaz-Graham (23 años y 2,13 m.) horas después de despedir a su hermano gemelo Jorge Díaz-Graham (23 años y 2,11 m.). No se dieron a conocer los detalles del contrato, pero la prensa de Dallas publica que se trata de un acuerdo de tipo 'Exhibit 10' igual al que firmó su hermano gemelo. Un contrato Exhibit 10 en la NBA es un vínculo laboral por una temporada, bajo el salario mínimo y sin dinero garantizado. Funciona como una cláusula de prueba de pretemporada. CBS Sports informa que si Guillermo Díaz-Graham es cortado antes del inicio de la temporada NBA todo apunta a que jugará para los Texas Legends de la G League (una situación idéntica a la de su hermano gemelo Jorge). Con esta decisión, tal y como publica Gigantes, los Dallas Mavericks pueden facilitar el paso de un jugador a su estructura de desarrollo y ofrecerle un incentivo económico sin necesidad de reservarle una plaza en la plantilla NBA. Jorge Díaz Graham (Oregon State) fue seleccionado en el Draft Internacional 2026 de la G-League con el número 1 por los Texas Legends, mientras que su hermano gemelo Guillermo Díaz Graham (San Francisco) fue seleccionado con el número 3 por el mismo equipo. El NBA G League International Draft es un draft específico creado para prospectos internacionales, separado del draft general de la G League. Los equipos que draftean a un jugador retienen sus derechos en la G League durante dos temporadas. Jorge Díaz Graham, que debutó en la pretemporada NBA con los Dallas Mavericks con 5 puntos, 3 rebotes y 1 asistencia en 12 minutos, es un ala-pívot canario de 23 años de edad y 2,11 metros, que destaca por su movilidad y capacidad de anotar desde lejos. Jugó en la cantera del La Laguna Tenerife hasta que dio el salto a Estados Unidos para jugar en MG Academy. Dio el salto a la NCAA para jugar tres temporadas en Pittsburgh y un último curso en Oregon State. Con los 'Beavers' promedió 6 puntos, 3,6 rebotes y 1 asistencia en 17,9 minutos. Por su parte su hermano gemelo Guillermo Díaz Graham (2,13 m.) siguió la misma trayectoria que Jorge, hasta que en su último año en la NCAA cambió Pittsburgh por San Francisco. Con los 'Dons' sus promedios fueron de 5,2 puntos, 3,2 rebotes y 1,3 asistencias en 17,2 minutos. Ha sido campeón de Europa sub-20 y ha sido convocado con la selección B de España.

articles.standfirst: Tony Parker: "Ahora sé por qué Andrés Feliz metió ocho triples... Estaba jugando contra su ídolo"
articles.summary: Tony Parker: "Ahora sé por qué Andrés Feliz metió ocho triples... Estaba jugando contra su ídolo"
articles.body: Tony Parker, entrenador del ASVEL Villeurbane que perdió 111-92 contra el Real Madrid en Euroliga, desveló por qué Andrés Feliz les acabó metiendo 8 triples. "Le pregunté a Andrés Feliz si iba a fallar un triple o algo por el estilo. Él me dice: 'Estoy jugando contra mi ídolo'", comentó en rueda de prensa el legendario base francés, que jugó 18 temporadas en la NBA y ganó cuatro anillos de campeón con los San Antonio Spurs de Popovich, Tim Duncan y Manu Ginóbili. El entrenador del ASVEL Villeurbane compartió en tono jocoso que "ahora entiendo por qué metió ocho triples... Estaba jugando contra su ídolo". Andrés Feliz, que fue el MVP del partido, terminó con 26 puntos, 4 rebotes, 5 asistencias y 30 de valoración. "Me siento bien. Sabemos del ritmo que quiere nuestro entrenador, cada día mejoramos, vamos adaptándonos. Y gracias a Dios nos van saliendo las cosas bien. Obviamente al principio siempre cuesta un poco adaptarse, pero creemos en el equipo, en el proyecto. Hay que seguir esa línea, creo que a largo plazo vamos a hacer un gran trabajo", declaró a los micrófonos de Movistar Plus+ al finalizar el partido. Sobre su actuación de MVP ante el ASVEL Villeurbane se sinceró reconociendo que "le doy gracias a Dios por el partido de hoy, a mis compañeros, a todos los entrenadores porque me han dado la confianza. Estoy contento de haber podido sacar la victoria, para nosotros era sumamente importante seguir en ese camino, seguir jugando bien y creyendo en el equipo. Hemos hecho un gran trabajo hoy". Andrés Feliz puso el broche a una excelente semana en lo individual en la Euroliga superando en sus dos partidos las mejores actuaciones que había completado hasta la fecha en el torneo. "Estoy orgulloso. Cada día trabajo para mejorar, pero sobre todo para ayudar al equipo. Gracias a Dios ha sido mi noche, como anteriormente lo ha sido la de otros compañeros. Me siento muy agradecido con mis compañeros, con la afición, con los entrenadores y con todo el mundo porque me han dado su apoyo y no me han dejado solo", apuntó. Contra el Armani Olimpia Milano firmó 15 puntos, 5 rebotes, 5 asistencias y 24 de valoración. Pedro Martínez también destacó el rendimiento del emergente Andrés Feliz: "ha jugado con muchísima determinación, sin dudar, con mucha confianza. Eso está muy bien. Hoy ha sido un jugador muy importante para nosotros porque ha metido unos tiros increíbles, muchos buenos tiros y con un porcentaje muy alto. Ha hecho un muy buen partido".

articles.title: La Euroliga repartirá 3.400 millones entre sus equipos
articles.standfirst: La competición hace oficial su plan de negocios para los próximos 10 años
articles.summary: La competición hace oficial su plan de negocios para los próximos 10 años
articles.body: En la trascendental Asamblea de propietarios de la Euroliga del pasado 6 de octubre a orillas del idílico Lago Como, los 13 equipos socios de la competición estudiaron y analizaron algunos asuntos de enorme calado, como la conversión de los equipos en franquicias, una inminente expansión y la oferta de la NBA de ir de forma conjunta, que desestimaron, acordando seguir negociando. Y entre todos esos temas, uno de ellos pasó algo más desapercibido porque no se dieron detalles. Ahora, la Euroliga los hace públicos y se trata del plan de negocios que vertebrará la competición en los próximos 10 años aprobado por los 13 dueños de la competición. En realidad, por su importancia, ese fue el tema más importante en el Lago Como, un plan que ahora ve la luz y que anuncia la propia Euroliga. Básicamente el plan de negocios de la Euroliga para la próxima década se basa en tres pilares fundamentales. Por un lado, la competición distribuirá la cifra de 3.400 millones de euros entre los equipos participantes en ese periodo de 10 años. Además, la Euroliga prevé alcanzar los 648 millones en ingresos comerciales llegado el décimo año. Y finalmente se estima que el valor conjunto de la Liga y sus equipos alcance los 13 billones de euros en la próxima década. Son cifras que asegurarían por completo la solidez y estabilidad de la competición a largo plazo. En su comunicado, la Euroliga explica que "el objetivo del plan es incrementar de forma significativa los ingresos comerciales de la Liga y la distribución de recursos económicos a los clubes participantes, al tiempo que se generan nuevas oportunidades de inversión y expansión". Además detalla que los 3.400 millones de euros a repartir entre los equipos, la cifra que más llama la atención del plan estratégico, se generan con "2.200 millones de euros procedentes de ingresos y 1.200 millones de euros derivados de las cuotas por franquicia". La Euroliga, en su plan de negocios, prevé un incremento de ingresos comerciales y con ello aumentará el reparto a sus socios. La idea que tienen es llegar a los 648 millones de euros en el décimo año: "Esta ambición se sustenta en la trayectoria de la Liga, que ha logrado multiplicar por cinco sus ingresos comerciales durante el periodo de 10 años anterior. Se prevé que la distribución económica a los clubes alcance los 2.200 millones de euros a lo largo de este periodo de 10 años, lo que refuerza el compromiso de la Liga de compartir el valor generado por la competición con los clubes participantes". Otra fuente de ingresos que se repartirá entre los equipos, según la Euroliga, son las cuotas generadas por las dos ventanas de expansión previstas para 2027 y 2031. La Euroliga detalla que tiene hasta 15 ofertas vinculantes con valor total de 1.200 millones de euros de equipos que quieren entrar en la competición: "Estas cantidades se sumarían a los ingresos comerciales distribuidos entre los clubes participantes, generando nuevas oportunidades para incrementar los recursos económicos disponibles en toda la Liga", dice la Euroliga. Con la transformación de los equipos en franquicias, la Euroliga espera que el valor previsto de la competición aumente en un 25%: "Al finalizar el horizonte temporal de 10 años, se proyecta que el valor conjunto de los actuales clubes con licencia alcance los 5.400 millones de euros —lo que supone triplicar su valor actual—, mientras que el valor de la Liga alcanzaría los 7.980 millones de euros, cifra equivalente a 5,7 veces su valoración estimada actual". En este ambicioso plan de negocio a 10 años, la Euroliga pretende "continuar centrándose en fortalecer los cimientos financieros de los clubes, apoyando el desarrollo de modelos de negocio sostenibles en toda la competición".
